title: Find Longest Special Substring That Occurs Thrice I
statement:
Call a string **special** when every character in it is the same letter, such as `"f"`, `"zz"` or `"ddd"` (but not `"abc"`).

Given a string `s` of lowercase English letters, find the longest special substring (a non-empty block of consecutive characters) that can be found in `s` starting at three or more different positions; the occurrences may overlap. Return its length, or `-1` if no special substring appears at least three times.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 50 characters, there are only about 1,275 substrings, so we can simply list them. And we only care about the special ones: from any starting position, a special substring keeps going exactly as long as the letter stays the same. Enumerate those, count how often each one shows up in a map, and the answer is the longest one with a count of at least three.

## Approach

1. For each `start`, extend `end` while `s[end]` equals `s[start]`, building `piece` one letter at a time.
2. Each `piece` is a special substring beginning at `start`; add one to its entry in `count`.
3. Afterwards, scan `count` and keep the greatest `piece.length` whose `occurrences` is at least 3 in `best`.
4. Return `best`, which stays `-1` when nothing qualifies.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "aaaa"`.

- `start = 0` adds `"a"`, `"aa"`, `"aaa"`, `"aaaa"`.
- `start = 1` adds `"a"`, `"aa"`, `"aaa"`.
- `start = 2` adds `"a"`, `"aa"`.
- `start = 3` adds `"a"`.

The counts are `"a"`: 4, `"aa"`: 3, `"aaa"`: 2, `"aaaa"`: 1. The longest piece seen three or more times is `"aa"`, so the answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n³) in the worst case (O(n²) special substrings, each built and hashed in O(n)); tiny for n ≤ 50.
- Space: O(n²) characters for the stored pieces in the worst case.

## Pitfalls

- Occurrences may overlap: `"aaaa"` contains `"aa"` three times, at positions 0, 1 and 2.
- Stop extending as soon as the letter changes, otherwise you count substrings that are not special.
- Return `-1`, not `0`, when no special substring appears three times.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | map from each special substring to how many positions it starts at |
| `start`, `end` | first and current last index of the substring being built |
| `piece` | the special substring `s[start..end]` |
| `occurrences` | how many times `piece` was found |
| `best` | longest qualifying length so far, `-1` if none |

narration.2: count maps each special substring to the number of places it starts.
narration.3: Try every position as the start of a special substring.
narration.5: Extend to the right only while the letter matches the starting letter.
narration.6: Grow the current special substring by one letter.
narration.7: Record one more occurrence of this exact substring.
narration.10: Start from -1, the answer when no special substring appears three times.
narration.11: Look at every special substring that was found.
narration.12: It qualifies only if it was found at three or more positions.
narration.16: Return the best length, or -1 if nothing qualified.
